headline: 10 killed in bus-truck collision in Natore, over 20 injured
summary: A head-on collision between an RP Paribahan bus and a sand-laden truck occurred early morning on the Pabna-Natore highway. Police and firefighters are on site, with the death toll feared to rise.
details: At least 10 people were killed and more than 20 injured in a head-on collision between a bus and a truck on Pabna-Natore highway near Natore's Bonpara early today.

The accident involved a Rajshahi-bound bus of RP Paribahan and a sand-laden truck, occurring around 4:00am. Sub-Inspector Md Alamgir Hossain of the Bonpara Highway Police Station confirmed the details.
All 10 confirmed victims were bus passengers, and authorities fear the death toll may still rise. The identities of the deceased have not yet been released.

Police and firefighters quickly responded to the scene to conduct rescue operations. The injured are receiving treatment at Natore General Hospital, Boraigram Upazila Health Complex, and other local medical facilities.
caption:

headline_marked: Prime Minister [[Tarique Rahman calls for unity]] among all religions to build Bangladesh
headline: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman calls for unity among all religions to build Bangladesh
summary: Speaking at Dhakeshwari National Temple during Durga Puja, the PM urged citizens to recognize each other as Bangladeshis first, recalling the spirit of the 1971 Liberation War and the July uprising.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman emphasized the importance of unity among people of all religions to collectively build Bangladesh. He stated that everyone should be recognized primarily as a Bangladeshi, transcending religious identity.

Addressing the Hindu community at the Dhakeshwari National Temple in Dhaka during Durga Puja, the Prime Minister declared, "This country belongs to you and me. Let's all work together, shoulder to shoulder, to build the country." He extended greetings for Durga Puja, calling it a celebration of joy and togetherness.

Rahman drew parallels to the 1971 Liberation War, noting that people fought for independence without regard for their fellow fighters' religious affiliations. He also referenced the July uprising, highlighting how people took to the streets united, irrespective of their religious backgrounds.

He urged continued unity for the nation's development, asserting that improvements in Bangladesh and its people's lives would benefit everyone. "When someone suffers, we do not look at their religion. Likewise, when people are doing well, we do not look at their religion. We see that you are human, and I am human," he added.
The Prime Minister called on citizens to recognize and respect one another as fellow human beings and integral members of Bangladesh.
Today, the Prime Minister is scheduled to visit puja mandaps in three districts: Rangpur in the morning, followed by Rajshahi and Chattogram.
caption:
